title: Three pillars, seven pebbles each
note: The page's three pillars of the Jamarat at Mina, numbered in the order they are stoned, seven pebbles above each.

lines.text: Twenty one pebbles a day, after the tenth
Mina, the tenth of Dhul Hijjah
On the tenth, seven at al-Aqabah alone
lines.sub: the large pillar, nearest to Makkah

lines.text: On 11 and 12, all three; on 13 if you stay
After the first two, a sunnah: make du'a
There is no devil standing at the pillars
Hanafis allow the thirteenth before noon
lines.sub: the other three require after noon each day

lines.text: Throw pebbles the size of a chickpea
Three pillars, named small, middle, large
lines.sub: one at a time, saying Allahu akbar

research.retell: At Mina the pilgrim throws seven pebbles at named stone pillars on set days, alone at the large one on the tenth and at all three afterward, in a fixed order.
proof: Twenty one pebbles a day.; three pillars, seven pebbles at each
the Jamarat; 10 Dhul Hijjah. Back to Mina at dawn: seven pebbles at the large pillar
on the 10th, this one alone; throw seven pebbles, one at a time, at the largest pillar, the one nearest Makkah... Today you throw at this one only, not at the other two.
on 11, 12 and 13, all three in order; stone the three pillars in order: the small one first, then the middle one, then the large one, seven pebbles at each, saying Allahu akbar with every throw.
stand and make du’a after the first two, and not after the third; After the large one, do not stop: he ﷺ threw at it and left without standing.
There is no devil standing at these pillars. The throwing is obedience and remembrance
Hanafi permit stoning before midday on the thirteenth day only; the other three schools require after midday on every day of Tashriq.
he ﷺ held up pebbles the size of beans and said: with the like of these, throw, and warned in the same breath against exaggeration in religion.
as-Sughra, the small; al-Wusta, the middle; al-Aqabah, the large; Hajj, day by day
